newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 23.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 23.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Monday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* The market will likely persist with its upward bias given the array of inexpensive issues to choose from but will react quickly to anything that appears to be bad news, Anscor-Hagedorn Securities analyst Jasmine Juanico said.
* The main index is likely to move within the 2,750 to 2,850 range as long as investors remain cautious in the light of the Thailand baht crisis, Sun Hung Kai Securities Phils said.
* On Friday, the Philippine composite index closed 24.24 points lower at 2,881.73 points.
* The Dow Jones on Friday ended 19.45 points higher at 7,796.51. PLDT's ADR closed $0 1/8 lower at $63 1/8.
* The Philippine peso closed lower at 26.38 to the dollar vs 26.372.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average rose to 15.03125 percent against 12.8125 percent.
* Philippine sugar miller Central Azucarera Don Pedro said it milled a record 1.5 million tonnes of cane for crop year 1996/1997 ending May 31.
* Metro Pacific Corp said it bought Filinvest Group's 16 percent stake in Bonifacio Land Corp for 5.36 billion pesos.

* A Reuters poll of five Manila brokerages showed that San Miguel Corp was expected to post a profit of 2.4 billion pesos, for the first half of the year, barely changed from 2.41 billion in the first six months of 1996.

* Music Semiconductors Corp said the Superior Court of New Jersey has upheld its rights over the assets of its unit Protelcon Inc, including patent rights over a television accessory called telecommander.

* State-controlled Land Bank of the Philipines said it has foreclosed some properties of North Negros Marketing Corp in partial payments of its debts worth 465.62 pesos. North Negros is the trading arm of sugar miller Victorias Milling Corp.
* Aboitiz Equity Ventures Inc said it has purchased an additional 16,459,680 of its own shares from an earlier 707,000 shares bought.
* The Central Bank raised overnight lending rate last Friday to 17 percent from 14.75 percent.
* A Philippines citizens group, PIRMA, said on Sunday it collected nearly six million signatures on a petition demanding constitutional change to let President Fidel Ramos run for re-election.
* Newspaper Philippine Star said PIRMA has asked the Commission on Elections (Comelec) to authenticate the signatures it has gathered.

* Manila Standard said Board of Investments figures showed that total investments in the country reached 271.12 billion in the first five months of the year, exceeding by 18 percent the target set by government.

* Creditors of Victorias Milling Co may be forced to foreclose mortgaged assets of the company following the failure of their meeting last Friday to fully resolve the issues that hinder a restructuring programme for the sugar miller.
* Manila Chronicle said Central Azucarera de Tarlac has embarked on a retrenchment programme in a bid to keep its business viable. Central has laid off 394 workers from its 1,800 workforce.

* Manila Bulletin said that the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co expects to generate additional revenues of about 7.0 billion pesos by end-1997 from 28.6 billion pesos in 1996 if it gets the approval of the National Telecommunications Commission for its proposed rate restructuring plan.
